page.layout: One printed page, one column. A centred title block at the top, then a 20-line acrostic poem with a letter column on the left and a letter column on the right. Below it, centred: a small label, a couplet, a second label, a pentameter line, and the date.

main_text.head: EPITAPHIVM CL. V. ac præstantissimi Theologi D. Petri Martyris Vermilij, sacrarum literarum in schola Tigurina professoris, scriptum per M. Balthazarum Susenbetum Eschuegensem Hassum.

p.i: Parua quidem Petri cineres modò Martyris urna
Excipit: at magnus vivit in orbe tamen.
Testis enim Christi, ceusydus in æthere, lumen
Resplendensq;, Dei fulsit in ipse domo.
Vidit eum Italiæ primum Florentia natum,
Sed locus ecce suos non fuit ullus apud.
Mox ad Germanos & ad Anglos mittitur exul,
A Maria sæua pellitur inde senex.
Rursus & hospitium Germania præbuit illi,
Testis ut æterni pergeret esse Dei.
Ὑ̓πεσθν[?] at bis sex ubi lustra peregerat, atque
Reddens tres annos martyrium absq; metu:
Vitæ pertæsus miserę, Christoq; vocanti,
E mundo in cœli gaudia lætus abit.
Reliquias igitur fragilis modo corporis urna
Marmoreo tumulo, concava mandat huic.
Illic fatali requiescunt membra sopore,
Longis qua mundi sunt agitata malis.
Ipsius at nomen fines penetrabit ad orbis
Vsque, simul laudis fama perennis erit.

main_text.head: DISTICHON, quod annum, mensem, & diem obitus eius ostendit.

p.i: Petrus, vt effulsit bis sexta luce Nouember, In cœli vectus iubila, Testis ouat.

main_text.head: PENTAMETER anni quo obijt numerum complectens.

p.i: Martyr vt astra petet, gens Tigurina dolet.

page.notes: The left and right margin letters are the acrostic letters: left P E T R V S M A R T Y R V E R M I L I VS, right A N N O M D L X I I E V I T A C E S S I T, each placed beside its verse line. The Greek word in line 11 is uncertain and marked [?]. "ceusydus" and "ecce suos" are printed without visible word spaces; I have followed the print. The date at the foot is read as MDLXII, which agrees with the acrostic, but the last strokes are hard to make out. Verse u/v spelling was normalised; the printed "viuit" was read as "vivit".
